subject: Getting Posterior Mean of a parameter up until current iteration while fitting the model

messages.author: 3b679b7acf28007c
messages.subject: Getting Posterior Mean of a parameter up until current iteration while fitting the model
parts:
Hi,

I'm jointly fitting two models with stan. Consider \beta as a parameter that is sampled from model1 and is used as a covariate in model2 (model 1 and model 2 are both in one stan code - you may consider them as two separate likelihood functions). Is there any way in Stan that while I'm running the model and sampling parameters, I can get posterior mean of \beta parameter up until this current iteration of MCMC? 

Please note that this is not calculating posterior mean after running the stan code. This, in fact, is getting posterior mean of a parameter up until this current iteration of MCMC while I'm still running the stan code.

Thanks very much for your help,
-Sepehr

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Getting Posterior Mean of a parameter up until current iteration while fitting the model
parts:
On Monday, February 29, 2016 at 8:44:56 AM UTC-5, sepehr akhavan wrote:
Please note that this is not calculating posterior mean after running the stan code. This, in fact, is getting posterior mean of a parameter up until this current iteration of MCMC while I'm still running the stan code.

Basically no. You can write the output to a CSV file and use a separate process to calculate the cumulative mean up to the last iteration written in the CSV file. You probably want to exclude the warmup period though.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting Posterior Mean of a parameter up until current iteration while fitting the model
parts:
Technically you can in CmdStan — because samples stream to 
the output CSV, running stansummary on an incomplete output
CSV will compute MCMC estimators up to that point.

Basically no. You can write the output to a CSV file and use a separate process to calculate the cumulative mean up to the last iteration written in the CSV file. You probably want to exclude the warmup period though.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Getting Posterior Mean of a parameter up until current iteration while fitting the model
parts:
But you can't get it in the Stan code itself.
Stan doesn't allow any reflection into runtime
properties. That's on purpose --- we want the
Stan program to define a log density that doesn't
depend on any state (other than the data, of course).

- Bob
